annotation.title_clean: Ethical Design of a Robot Platform for Disabled Employees: Some Practical Methodological Considerations
annotation.title_en: Ethical Design of a Robot Platform for Disabled Employees: Some Practical Methodological Considerations
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Colombino, T.; Gallo, D.; Shreepriya, S.; Im, Y.; Cha, S.
annotation.summary_en: Research paper describing an ethnography and design-fiction approach used with a Korean business employing people with developmental disabilities to develop robot-platform scenarios. It argues that a priori ethical stances like inclusivity are risky and that organizational and bureaucratic context and stakeholder perspectives must shape ethical HRI design.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethnography and design fictions help surface unintended consequences of introducing robots for vulnerable workers.
A priori ethical prescriptions such as inclusivity may conflict with stakeholder perspectives.
Organizational hierarchies, business models and operating philosophy must be considered in HRI scenario design.
Disabled employees are weakly represented in design; managers act as gatekeepers and proxies.
Questions who has authority to decide what well-being means and what degree of automation is appropriate.
